article.title: Brent crude climbs to a five-month high on tightening OPEC+ supply
article.text: Brent crude settled at a five-month high after OPEC+ signalled it would hold production cuts through the next quarter, tightening global supply as demand stayed resilient.
article.note: HINDOILEXP shape, isolated: the mapping stage proposes a micro-cap explorer purely because its NAME and SECTOR resemble the real upstream-realization beneficiaries -- 'oil exploration' pattern-matches the mechanism prior even though the company's actual commercial output is negligible. The semantic counterfactual verifier is the safeguard that must catch this, not the gate: a plausible-sounding rationale and a real sector/name match are not evidence of a material, event-specific relationship.

companies.rationale: Genuine producing E&P with crude-linked realizations, but small output base and gas-weighted mix limit absolute earnings impact.

reject.reason: Micro-cap explorer with negligible commercial crude output; realization-uplift mechanism is not material at the corporate level and inclusion rests mainly on sector/name similarity to the real upstream producers (ONGC, Oil India) rather than on this company's own economics. Effect too immaterial for a professional impact graph on an unquantified crude move.

ground_truth.rationale: HINDOILEXP genuinely operates in the same sub-sector as the real upstream beneficiaries and the mapping stage's rationale reads plausibly on its face -- this is exactly what makes it a semantic-similarity false positive rather than an obviously bad candidate. The verifier is the safeguard that must catch it: the company's own commercial output is too small for a benchmark crude move to be a material, event-specific story, and the verifier explicitly names sector/name-pattern-matching (not this company's own economics) as the actual basis for the proposal. A plausible mechanism sentence and a genuine sector match are not evidence -- the candidate must be absent from every tier.
